_note: B-29. IdentityOps PowerShell levers over the offline mock tenant (fixtures/tenant/<client>.json and <client>/sessions.json). Graph permission names in graph_scopes are the least-privilege set a real adapter would be reviewed against; they are UNVERIFIED except where levers/powershell/IdentityOps/README.md says otherwise. Mock only; no real tenant is called.

levers.name: user.revoke-sessions
levers.description: Revoke a member user's sign-in sessions (refresh tokens) so they must sign in again. Mock of Graph revokeSignInSessions. Takes effect after a documented lag and does not apply to guest users.

impact.L1: One person is signed out of every app and must sign in again; unsaved work in open apps can be lost, and access tokens may work for a short while longer.
impact.L2: The client cuts off a possibly stolen session without disabling the account; a wrong target interrupts that person's day.
impact.L3: A containment step the MSP can show an auditor: dry-run diff, lead approval, audit record; the lag is stated up front so nobody over-promises.
impact.L4: Fast, repeatable session revocation limits the damage from a stolen sign-in at every client, not just the one that noticed.

levers.name: user.enable
levers.description: Enable a user account (accountEnabled = true). The undo of user.disable. Mock of a Graph user update.

impact.L1: One person can sign in again; a wrong target or an impostor's request gives the wrong person access.
impact.L2: The client gets a mistaken disable fixed, or restores a returning employee; a wrong enable reopens an account that was closed on purpose.
impact.L3: Re-enabling is the other half of offboarding: verified requester, lead approval, audit record, and it reverses user.disable exactly.
impact.L4: A fast, safe undo makes people willing to automate containment, which protects every client.

levers.name: user.set-properties
levers.description: Change one directory property of a user for a mover: department, jobTitle or manager. Nothing else can be changed with this lever. Mock of a Graph user update.

value.description: New department or job title, or the new manager's userPrincipalName

impact.L1: One person's department, title or manager changes in the directory; group-based access that follows those fields can change with it.
impact.L2: The client's address book, approvals and dynamic access follow the new values; a wrong manager sends approvals to the wrong person.
impact.L3: A mover step the MSP can show an auditor: only three fields, dry-run diff, lead approval, and set the old value back with the same lever.
impact.L4: Movers are where leftover access piles up; changing the fields in one tested path keeps that cleanup the same at every client.
